PLAYTEST REPAIR · USER ISSUE 2 / VISUAL ISSUE 5 · 11 NOVEMBER 2026

A fairer strike.
A clearer reaction.

Slap a Mole now catches bounded motion between fresh palm/foot observations and announces arrivals before the reaction window. Distinct local visual cues make targets, bombs and their outcomes readable over raw camera imagery.

Issue #62 · Pull request link will be added after local validation. · Owning design

What changed and why

  • 450ms READY / BOMB SOON warning, then the full lifetime. Easy stays 5 seconds, Normal 4, Hard 3. Warnings accept no strikes and spend none of that lifetime. All target clocks freeze on interruption.
  • A bounded straight segment in canonical source coordinates. Touch requires the same named palm or foot in adjacent samples, at most 120ms apart and at most 0.30 image units of travel. Existing contact/target radii stay unchanged. Both endpoints may miss while the intervening segment crosses the target.
  • Fresh intentional entry. A segment must start outside the combined region. Warning-time motion is clipped at actual activation; stationary-on-spawn, missing-limb return, stale input, pauses, identity/revision breaks and excessive gaps/jumps earn nothing. Slow entry remains usable without a minimum speed.
  • Spatial outcomes. +points, −50, ESCAPED and SAFE persist for 650 active ms, capped at 12 events. HIT/AVOID text, explicit BOMB SOON warnings, dashed arrival borders and local backplates distinguish phases without tinting camera pixels. Reduced motion disables the brief impact-scale animation.
  • Dodgeball visuals only. A local outline and MOVE CLEAR / DANGER / CONTACT / CLEAR labels improve contrast. Its collision policy and timing are unchanged.

Tradeoff: the bounded segment approximates a straight path between observations. Curved or longer unobserved movement is not reconstructed. Deliberate slow entry is accepted; real-world jitter, body scale and sensitivity still require participant trials. Expirations resolve before collisions, so a late sample cannot revive a target.

Scope and remaining gates

This is software evidence. No camera exposure synchronization, physical responsiveness, participant reach/comfort, palm accuracy, hardware throughput or multiplayer certification was measured. No participant video or training data was supplied; no models, weights, camera acquisition, shared session/vision or enrollment logic changed.

The bounded source policy is conservative software tuning. Very fast movement beyond the bound and long gaps are rejected intentionally. The existing 350ms general freshness policy and unknown transport offset remain. Tests and screenshots do not establish motion-to-display latency.

Related merged rules reviewed: #49 bombs and lifetimes, #57 rig composition, #58 palm/foot regions. This focused branch is independent of the other playtest repair sets. PR is not merged by this task.
